topStories.headline: Hundreds Turn Out Against Developer-Led Town East of Heber — Philo Now Has a Year to Decide
topStories.dek: Residents packed a state-hosted public hearing on the proposed Wasatch Highlands preliminary municipality, with elected officials and neighbors united in opposition.
topStories.body:
More than 30 people stepped to the microphone at Wasatch High School Auditorium on October 27 to voice objections to Wasatch Highlands, a 2,700-acre proposed development east of Heber City that is pursuing incorporation as a so-called preliminary municipality under Senate Bill 258, a 2024 state law. The hearing was hosted by the Utah Lieutenant Governor's Office, which will ultimately decide whether Wasatch Highlands can incorporate — a process that, unlike conventional town formation, does not require a public vote.

Philo Development's Greg Whitehead is the primary sponsor of the proposal. The company previously sought annexation into Heber City and approval from Wasatch County, and was turned away by both. A feasibility study by consulting firm LRB Finance Advisors found that the proposed town could be economically viable and could support up to 2,200 residents at build-out, though most public commenters flatly rejected that conclusion.

Heber City Mayor Heidi Franco and City Councilmember Yvonne Barney were among the elected officials who spoke against the project. Wasatch County, Summit County, and the town of Wallsburg have all formally called on the Legislature to repeal SB 258, and Wasatch County has filed court papers supporting a Moab-based lawsuit arguing that preliminary municipalities are unconstitutional. Following Tuesday's hearing, Philo Development has one year to formally decide whether to proceed with incorporation.

topStories.headline: Heber City Seals North Fields Pact With Wasatch County, Blocking Annexation of Wetland Farmland
topStories.dek: Both governments have now signed a memorandum of understanding that keeps the beloved North Fields out of Heber City's expansion boundary.
topStories.body:
After months of negotiation, Heber City voted unanimously at its October 21 council meeting to adopt a memorandum of understanding with Wasatch County that formally protects the North Fields — a freshwater wetland and agricultural area northwest of downtown that residents often call the crown jewel of Heber Valley. Wasatch County had adopted its side of the agreement at a council meeting on October 7, making the pact official with both signatures now in place.

City Manager Matt Brower described the memorandum as having three parts: obligations specific to Heber City, obligations specific to the county, and shared guidelines. The county commits to zoning the North Fields only for rural agricultural uses, while Heber City commits to keeping the area outside its annexation boundary — specifically, not extending development past 850 North on the west side of U.S. Highway 40. The city also agreed to direct unit-based preservation fees collected from development in the North Village area toward land acquisition and conservation easements in the North Fields.

The agreement arrives ahead of a final environmental impact decision by the Utah Department of Transportation on its preferred Heber Valley Corridor bypass route, which would cut through portions of the North Fields. Wasatch County, Midway City, and some Heber City council members have submitted a joint letter to UDOT opposing that route. City and county officials said they also plan to negotiate a more legally binding interlocal agreement to further cement North Fields protections.

topStories.headline: Election Day Is Tuesday: Six County Races on the Ballot, Including a New Sheriff
topStories.dek: Wasatch County voters head to the polls November 3 to fill the sheriff's seat and five other county offices, with in-person voting available at the county administration building in Heber City.
topStories.body:
With incumbent Sheriff Jared Rigby having been indicted by a grand jury and eliminated in the June primary, Tuesday's general election will produce a new Wasatch County Sheriff for the first time in years. Republican nominee Jeremy Hales, the county's former emergency management director, faces unaffiliated candidate Paul Moore. Hales won the June 23 primary with roughly 66 percent of Republican votes.

The November 3 ballot also includes races for county attorney, clerk-auditor, and County Council seats A, C, and F. In-person voting runs from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. at the Wasatch County Administration Building, 25 N. Main St., Heber City. Ballot drop boxes are located at Charleston Town Hall, Hideout Town Hall, the Wasatch County Administration Building, the Wasatch County Library, Midway City Hall, and Wallsburg Town Hall. Mail-in ballots must reach the Clerk-Auditor's Office by 8 p.m. on election night. Same-day voter registration is available at the polls.

moreNews.headline: Heber Valley Temple Construction Presses On While Utah Supreme Court Deliberates
moreNews.body: Work on the Heber Valley Utah Temple continues along E. Center Street in Heber City, with basement walls rising from an excavated pit on the roughly 18-acre site. A final opinion from the Utah Supreme Court — which is deciding whether the temple is permitted to be built at all — had not been issued as of mid-October. Observers familiar with the case said a decision was unlikely before the end of October and could take one to two more months. If the court rules against the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and Wasatch County, the structure would have to be torn down and the land restored.

moreNews.headline: Community Blood Drive at Wasatch Fire District Runs Through November 15
moreNews.body: ARUP Blood Services is collecting donations at the Wasatch Fire District Community Room, 251 E. 1200 S., Heber City, through November 15. Donors are asked to make an appointment in advance by calling 801-584-5272. Walk-ins may be accommodated based on availability.
